divergences.old: Reading --project and --repo context from the first git remote on the connection's host in `git remote -v` order, which is sorted by remote name
divergences.toil: origin is offered first, then the other remotes in that order, and the first on the connection's host wins. The two differ only when origin and a remote whose name sorts before it (mirror, fork) are both on the host
divergences.why: origin is the clone's own remote, so it's the least surprising one to act on when two remotes point at the same server.

divergences.old: "Could not determine Bitbucket project/repo. Pass --project and --repo, or run config init." (and the project-only form for repo create and pr create-many)
divergences.toil: The same first sentence, then "or set project and repo on the connection", with a fix naming the env vars; checked by core before the command runs, so for pr list it comes before a bad --created-after is reported
divergences.why: toil has no config init; an error must point at something the user can do.

divergences.old: git current-pr with no Bitbucket baseUrl or token returning { message: "Requires Bitbucket config. Available after config init." }
divergences.toil: The same success with a message, now "Requires Bitbucket config. Available after toil connections add."; a connection that exists but lacks pat also adds a CONFIG_INCOMPLETE warning naming the key
divergences.why: toil has no config init, so the message names the command that sets a connection up.

divergences.old: pr list, pr comments paging until isLastPage is true, stepping by start + limit when a page has no nextPageStart, with no limit on the number of pages
divergences.toil: Paging stops when isLastPage is true or a page has no nextPageStart, and after 1,000 pages (100,000 items) fails with HTTP naming the list and a fix to narrow it
divergences.why: A server that never says isLastPage would otherwise be read forever; Bitbucket sends nextPageStart on every page that isn't the last.

divergences.old: Project key, repository slug, user slug, commit and the pr diff --file path put into request paths as typed (only repo default-reviewers encoded project and repo), so an id with path syntax in it, such as a / ? or #, changed or cut the path
divergences.toil: Each id is encoded as one path segment, and the --file path one segment at a time, with a . or .. part refused as INVALID_INPUT; project and repo holding /, \, ?, #, % or a control character are refused as INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, wherever the value came from (flag, connection, dossier, env or git remote)
divergences.why: An id names one resource. Bitbucket project keys are letters, digits and _ (a personal project is ~ and a URL-safe user slug) and repository slugs are letters, digits, -, _ and ., so no real key or slug holds those characters, and a file name holding # or ? is still that file.

divergences.old: pr diff <id>, the pull request id a required argument
divergences.toil: pr diff [id], optional, because a Cloud connection can diff a commit spec (--spec) instead of a pull request. Data Center still requires it: a call without an id is INVALID_INPUT naming the missing argument, before any request
divergences.why: Bitbucket Data Center and Bitbucket Cloud are one area now (#495), so one command has one argument list, and it can't be required for one deployment and optional for the other. Data Center's behavior is the contract's.
